Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verses 13–14:

His saying, may He be exalted and majestic: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾. In ﴿ordained for you﴾ there are four meanings:

One: He prescribed (sanna) for you.

Second: He made clear (bayyana) for you.

Third: He chose (ikhtara) for you. This is said by al-Kalbi.

Fourth: He made obligatory (awjaba) upon you.

﴿Of the religion﴾ means the religion, and "min" (of) is extra (za'ida) in the speech.

In ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ there are two meanings:

One of them: the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, because he was the first prophet to bring his community the prohibition of that. This is said by al-Hakam.

Second: the permitting of what is lawful and the forbidding of what is unlawful. This is said by Qatadah.

﴿And what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: act upon it. This is said by al-Suddi.

Second: call to it.

Mujahid said: the religion of God is one in obedience to Him and in His oneness.

It may also bear a third meaning: strive against those who oppose it.

﴿And do not be divided therein﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: do not transgress against one another over it, and be brothers in it. This is said by Abu al-Aliyah.

Second: do not differ concerning it, for every prophet confirms the one before him. This is said by Muqatil.

﴿Grievous to the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾. Qatadah said: it is the testimony that there is no god but God.

It may also be that it refers to acknowledging His prophethood, since it is more burdensome to them and they are more averse to it.

﴿God chooses for it whom He wills﴾, to the end of the verse.

In it there are two meanings:

One of them: "He chooses for it whom He wills" refers to those born upon Islam. ﴿And guides to it whoever turns back﴾ refers to those who embrace Islam from polytheism. This is said by al-Kalbi.

Second: "He selects for it whom He wills," said by Mujahid; and "He guides to it whoever turns to His obedience," said by al-Suddi.

His saying, may He be exalted and majestic: ﴿And they did not become divided﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: concerning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Second: concerning the Qur'an.

﴿Except after knowledge had come to them﴾. In it there are three meanings:

One: except after they had delved deeply into knowledge. This is said by al-A'mash.

Second: except after they knew that division is misguidance. This is said by Ibn Ziyad.

Third: except after the Qur'an had come to them, and it is called knowledge because it is learned from.

﴿Out of mutual rivalry among themselves﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: for the pursuit of worldly life and the seeking of its dominion. This is said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Second: because some of them transgressed against others. This is said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

(p-198)﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: concerning His mercy toward people despite their wrongdoing.

Second: concerning the postponement of their punishment. This is said by Qatadah.

﴿Until a specified term﴾: until the Hour is established, for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾, to the end of the verse.

It may also mean until the term at which their punishment has been decreed.

﴿The matter would have been decided between them﴾, i.e., their destruction would have been hastened.

﴿And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them﴾. Concerning them there are two sayings:

One of them: they are the Jews and the Christians. This is said by al-Suddi.

Second: they are those who were informed after the prophets. This is said by al-Rabi'.

﴿Are in doubt concerning it, unsettling doubt﴾. In it there are three meanings:

One of them: they are in doubt concerning the Qur'an. This is said by al-Rabi'.

Second: they are in doubt concerning sincerity. This is said by Abu al-Aliyah.

Third: they are in doubt concerning the truthfulness of the Messenger. This is said by al-Suddi.

The second: so seek (its acceptance).

In ﴿And be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ there are three interpretations: First, be steadfast in obeying God's command, said by Qatadah.

The third: so be steadfast in conveying the message, said by al-Dahhak.

First: there is no enmity between us and you, said by Mujahid. Al-Suddi said: this was before the sword, and before being commanded to pay the jizya (the poll tax on non-Muslim subjects).

The second: its meaning is that, since you have shown hostility, you have turned away from seeking proof, said by Ibn 'Isa.

The third: its meaning is that we have already been excused by establishing the proof against you, so there is no argument between us and you that we need to establish against you.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verse 16–18:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those who argue about Allah﴾ — concerning this there are two opinions:

One of them: concerning the Oneness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: they are the Jews, who said: "Our Book came before your Book, and our prophet came before your prophet, and we are better than you." This is related from Qatadah.

﴿After it has been responded to﴾ — concerning this there are three aspects:

One of them: after Allah has granted him (the Prophet) the manifestation of the miracles.

The second: after Allah has responded to the Messenger in the argument.

The third: after the Muslims have responded to their Lord and believed in His Book and His Messenger. This is related from Ibn Zayd.

﴿Their argument is futile﴾ — concerning this there are two aspects:

One of them: it is false (bāṭilah). This is related from Ibn ʿĪsā.

The second: it is losing (khāsirah). This is related from Ibn Zayd.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth﴾ — concerning this there are two aspects:

One of them: with the miraculous proof that attests to its authenticity.

The second: with truthfulness in what it reports of the past and the future.

﴿And the Balance﴾ — concerning this there are three aspects:

One of them: that it is the recompense for obedience with reward and for disobedience with punishment.

The second: that it is justice in what He has commanded and what He has forbidden. This is related from Qatadah.

The third: that it is the balance by which things are weighed, which Allah sent down from the sky and taught His servants to weigh with, so that there would be no oppression or defrauding among them. Qatadah said: "The Balance is justice."

﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ — He did not inform him of it, and He did not feminize (qarīb) because the feminine gender of as-sāʿah (the Hour) is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī), since it is like a time (waqt).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verse 23–24:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for (my) kinsfolk﴾. Concerning this there are five interpretations:

The first: its meaning is that you should not harm me in my person on account of my kinship with you. This applies specifically to the Quraysh, because there was no clan of the Quraysh without a kinship tie between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, Mujahid, and Abu Malik.

The second: its meaning is, except that you should fulfil my kinship (ʾadaa qarabati, i.e., honour the ties of kinship owed to me). This is the view of ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, and al-Suddi.

Miqsam narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard something bad, so he delivered a sermon and said to the Ansar: (Were you not humble, and did Allah not make you mighty through me? Were you not astray, and did Allah not guide you through me? Were you not fearful, and did Allah not grant you security through me?) Whenever he said something, they would say (Allah and His Messenger are most gracious). Then he said: Will you not answer me? They said: With what shall we answer you? He said: You should say: (Did your people not expel you, and we sheltered you? Did your people not deny you, and we affirmed you?) He kept enumerating them to them. He said: So they fell on their knees and said: Our souls and our wealth are yours." Then there was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for (my) kinsfolk﴾.

The third: its meaning is, except that you should show affection and support to me as you show affection and support to your own kinsmen. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: its meaning is, except that you should seek affection and draw near to Allah through obedience and righteous deeds. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The fifth: its meaning is, except that you should love your kinsfolk and maintain your ties of kinship. This was said by ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Qasim.

﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾, i.e., acquires it; the root of al-qarf is al-kasb (acquisition).

﴿We increase for him therein in goodness﴾, i.e., We multiply for him the good deed tenfold.

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Appreciative﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One of them: He forgives sins and appreciates good deeds. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: He forgives the sins of the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and appreciates their good deeds. This was said by al-Suddi.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal over your heart﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: i.e., He would make you forget what He has given you of the Qur'an. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: its meaning is that He would bind your heart so that harm does not reach it through their saying, "He has fabricated a lie against Allah." This was said by Muqatil.

The third: its meaning is that if you were to entertain in your soul the notion of fabricating a lie against Allah, Allah would seal your heart. This was said by Ibn ʿIsa.

﴿And Allah establishes the truth by His words﴾. This may bear two interpretations:

One of them: He supports His religion by His promise.

The second: He confirms His Messenger by His revelation.

The utterance of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

First: it refers to the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd, the fixed penalties) for acts of disobedience. This was said by al-Ḥasan.

Second: it refers to trials affecting the self and property, as a punishment for acts of disobedience and sins.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: « (No harm befalls the son of Adam, not a scratch from a stick, nor a stumble of a foot, nor a twitch of a vein, except for a sin, and He pardons more than that)». And Thābit al-Bunānī said:

It used to be said: "The hours of harm wipe away the hours of sins."

Then concerning this there are two opinions:

First: it is specific to adults, that it is a punishment for them, and for children that it is a reward for them.

Second: it is a general punishment for adults in their own persons, and for children in respect of others, such as a father or a mother. This was said by al-‘Alā' ibn Zayd.

﴿And He pardons much﴾. Concerning it there are two aspects:

First: He pardons many of the sins so that no prescribed penalties (ḥudūd) are imposed for them. This is what the saying of al-Ḥasan implies.

Second: He pardons many of the disobedient and does not hasten to punish them.

‘Alī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "What Allah punishes for in this world, Allah is too forbearing to repeat the punishment for it on the Day of Resurrection; and what Allah has pardoned in this world, Allah is too generous to revoke His pardon on the Day of Resurrection."(p-٢٠٥)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verse 32–35:

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And among His signs are the ships sailing through the sea like mountains.﴾ Mujahid said: they are the ships in the sea. ﴿Like mountains⦆ means like mountains. From this is the saying of al-Khansa':

"Indeed Sakhr, the guided ones take him as their guide; it is as if he were a banner with fire atop it."

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface.﴾ That is, standing still on the surface of the water. Qatadah said: because the ships of this sea travel by the wind, so when it is withheld from them, they become motionless.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person.﴾ Steadfast (sabbar) in trials, grateful (shakur) for blessings.

Qutrub said: How excellent is the servant who is steadfast and grateful, who gives thanks when he is given, and endures when he is tested.

Awn ibn Abd Allah said: How many a person bestowed upon is not grateful, and how many a person tested is not patient.

﴿Or He destroys them for what they have earned﴾: its meaning is that He drowns them for the sins of their people.

﴿And He pardons much﴾ of them, so He does not drown them along with it.

﴿They have no place of refuge.﴾ Regarding this there are two views:

The first: no escape or place to flee to, said by Qutrub.

The second: no refuge, said by al-Suddi, derived from their saying "haasa bihi al-ba'ir haysatan" (the camel swerved with him in a swerve) when it veered with him; and from this the saying "fulan yahis 'an al-haqq" (so-and-so swerves away from the truth), meaning he turns away from it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verses 36–39:

﴿And they establish the prayer﴾ Regarding it there are two views:

First: it means guarding its appointed times (mawaqit), said by Qatadah.

Second: completing it with its conditions (shurut), said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

﴿And their affair is by consultation among themselves﴾ Regarding it there are four views:

First: before the coming of the Prophet ﷺ to them, when they wished to do something, they would consult about it and then act upon it, so Allah praised them for it, said by al-Naqqash.

Second: meaning that, in their submission to sound opinion in their affairs, they were in agreement and did not differ, so they were praised for the unity of their word. Al-Hasan said: "No people ever consulted among themselves except that they were guided to the most rightful of their affairs."

Third: it refers to their consultation when they heard of the emergence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the arrival of the nuqaba' (chieftains/representatives) to them, until their opinion converged in the house of Abu Ayyub on faith in him and support for him, said by al-Dahhak.

Fourth: that they consult regarding whatever matters arise for them, so that none of them monopolizes good to the exclusion of others.

﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ Regarding it there are two views:

First: it means paying the zakat from their wealth, said by al-Suddi.

Second: spending from the lawful (halal) earnings they have, and this is a possibility.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who, when wrong (al-baghy) afflicts them, defend themselves﴾ Regarding it there are three sayings:

First: "afflicts them" refers to the polytheists over their religion; they defended themselves against them with the sword, said by Ibn Jurayj.

Second: "afflicts them" refers to one who oppresses them; he disliked that they be humiliated, so when they were able, they pardoned, said by Ibrahim.

Third: when wrong afflicts them, they support one another against it until they remove it from them and repel it from them, said by Ibn Bahr.

"The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills﴾. ʿUbayda said: He bestows females upon whom He wills, with no males among them, and He bestows males upon whom He wills, with no females among them.

He applied the alif (the feminine-marking "ā" ending, i.e., the indefinite form) to the males without the females, because they are more noble, so He distinguished them with the mark of definiteness.

﴿Or He couples them, males and females﴾. In this there are two views:

The first: she gives birth to a boy, then a girl, then a boy, then a girl. This is the view of Mujahid.

The second: she gives birth to twins, a boy and a girl. This is the view of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. Here, "coupling" (tazwij) means combining sons and daughters.

Ibn Qutayba said: The Arabs say "my camels coupled me" (zawwajanī ibilī) when they gather together the young and the old.

﴿And He makes whom He wills barren﴾, that is, he will not have offspring.

It is said: "her womb became barren of childbearing," meaning it was prevented.

Al-Naqqash related that this verse was revealed specifically concerning the prophets, though its ruling is general. Thus He gave Lot daughters with no male among them, He gave Abraham males with no female with them, He gave Isma'il and Isaac both males and females, and He made ʿIsa and Yahya barren."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 42, verses 51–53:

The occasion of its revelation is what al-Naqqash related: the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Will you not speak with God and look upon Him, if you are a truthful prophet, just as Moses spoke with Him and looked upon Him?" So this verse was revealed.

Regarding His words ﴿wahyan﴾ (by revelation) there are two views:

The first: it is a breath (nafth) breathed into his heart, so that it becomes inspiration (ilham). This was said by Mujahid.

The second: a dream he sees in his sleep. This was said by Zuhayr ibn Muhammad.

﴿Or from behind a veil﴾ — Zuhayr said: as He spoke to Moses.

﴿Or He sends a messenger﴾ — Zuhayr said: he is Jibril.

﴿So that he reveals by His permission what He wills﴾ — and this revelation from the messengers is an address from them to the prophets, who hear it as speech and see it as direct vision.

Thus was the state of Jibril when he descended with revelation to the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Abbas said: Jibril descended to every prophet, but none of them saw him except Muhammad, Isa, Musa and Zakariyya, peace and blessings of God be upon them all. As for others, it was revelation by inspiration in a dream.

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ — concerning it there are three interpretations:

The first: a mercy from Us, said by Qatadah.

The second: revelation from Our command, said by al-Suddi.

The third: the Qur'an from Our command, said by al-Dahhak.

﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ — concerning it there are two views:

The first: you did not know what the Book was without the message, nor faith without maturity (bulugh), said by Ibn Isa.

The second: you did not know what the Book was without Our bounty upon you, nor faith without Our guidance to you, and this is a possibility.

Concerning this "faith" there are two views:

The first: that it is faith in God, which he came to know after maturity and before prophethood.

The second: that it is the religion of Islam, which he did not know until after prophethood.

﴿But We made it a light﴾ — concerning it there are two statements:

The first: We made the Qur'an a light, said by al-Suddi.

(p-213) The second: We made faith a light.

Related by al-Naqqash, and said by al-Dahhak.

﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path﴾ — concerning it there are two statements:

The first: its meaning is, "And indeed you call to a straight religion," said by Qatadah.

The second: "to a straight Book," said by Ali, may God be pleased with him.

ʿAsim al-Jahdari read: ﴿wa innaka latuhda﴾ with a dammah on the ta', meaning latud'a (you are called).

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿the path of God﴾ — concerning it there are two views:

The first: that the path of God is the Qur'an, said by Ali, may God ennoble his face.

The second: Islam, narrated by al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari from the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿Surely to God all matters return﴾ — this admits of two interpretations:

The first: that it is a warning of resurrection (ba'th).

The second: that it is a warning of recompense (jaza'), and God knows best.
